blurTest.evidence: The upgrade headline, lifetime action, monthly alternative, and legal footer retain a clear priority order at gallery scale.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The centered purchase card is visually distinct from the picker workspace while retaining NameSnap's rounded, playful visual language.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: A user can immediately identify the free limit, monthly renewal, lifetime option, restoration path, and dismissal action.

realityTest.evidence: The rendered prices match the StoreKit fallback values, the monthly cadence is explicit, and no fabricated testimonial or outcome appears.

journeyTest.evidence: The modal supports purchase, restore, dismissal, privacy review, and Terms review without leaving an ambiguous dead end.

platformTest.evidence: The SwiftUI view was rendered on an iPhone 17 Pro at standard and Accessibility Extra Large text sizes; content scrolls while the legal links stay visible.

buyerValueTest.evidence: Unlimited contestants, no-account use, restoration, exact purchase cadence, and one-time versus recurring pricing are stated directly.

implementationTest.evidence: Debug and Release simulator builds succeeded with build 11; both policy URLs are real HTTPS destinations and the UI-test route is DEBUG-only.

screenFindings: Independent critique found no App Store marketing-frame leakage: this reads as a functional purchase decision inside the picker, not a screenshot caption.
The custom display face is confined to high-emphasis controls; explanatory and legal copy use readable system typography.
At Accessibility Extra Large, purchase content remains scrollable and the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use remain persistently available.
repairs: Added the Apple Standard EULA and Privacy Policy as visible paywall actions.
Added explicit monthly renewal and lifetime one-time-purchase disclosure plus per-month price labeling.
Changed the modal to adaptive scrolling, stacked accessibility actions, and a fixed legal footer; removed underlying toolbar bleed-through.
verdict: Approved for build 11. The paywall is legible, purchase terms are explicit, legal links remain visible, and the previous EULA omission is corrected in both the binary and listing metadata.
